item.title: Delaware couple wins HOA garage dispute as court orders removal of property violation notice
item.description: John and Sandra Mitchell have won a court case against their homeowners association regarding garage construction plans. They proposed a 24-by-28-foot garage with metal siding, which the board initially rejected. The court ruled that the association overstepped its authority by denying the materials without clear restrictions. The violation notice against their property was ordered to be removed from public records.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Trump gears up for Iran escalation after US polls; Tehran says position unchanged
item.description: US President Donald Trump has signaled potential military action against Iran following the upcoming midterm elections. The US has increased its military presence in the Persian Gulf with additional aircraft and troops. Iran is reportedly preparing for retaliation against US and allied interests in the region. Both Trump and Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu may view renewed conflict as a political strategy.

item.title: Kentucky court halts inquiry into widow's mental capacity after she rejects late husband's will
item.description: A Kentucky appeals court ruled that a district court could not investigate Tamara Williams' mental capacity claim. The dispute arose over her choice to reject her late husband Julian D. Williams' will for a statutory share. After her husband's death, Tamara's decision was contested by his stepchildren, who claimed she lacked mental capacity. The appeals court determined that contested cases must be resolved in circuit court rather than district court.

item.title: George Harrison donated his album royalties to charity. In 2024, his foundation spent £573,221
item.description: George Harrison's Material World Foundation continues to thrive, providing substantial funding to charitable initiatives worldwide. In 2024 alone, the foundation allocated over £573,000 towards public health, education, and emergency relief efforts. Operated independently by a board of trustees including Olivia Harrison, it eschews salaries to focus all resources on its mission. Founded from royalties of Harrison's classic album, Living in the Material World, the foundation's influence endures, promoting lasting change.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Kansas appeals court reopens divorce property case after jailed husband missed hearing next door
item.description: A Kansas appeals court recently vacated a previous ruling in a divorce property case, asserting that Scott L. Hale was not given a fair chance to participate. Haltingly unable to attend his hearing due to incarceration, Scott's objections to the property division were overlooked by the trial judge. The court's decision sends the matter back to the lower court for a comprehensive reassessment and new hearing.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: 80-ton boulder collapses at park after 104 years, smashing a walkway but injuring no one
item.description: In a surprising turn of events on October 18, 2026, an 80-ton granite boulder collapsed at Polar Caves Park in Rumney, New Hampshire, smashing a wooden walkway and its safety rails. Fortunately, this incident resulted in no injuries. The boulder's fall is likely due to weather-related erosion. Park authorities are now assessing the situation and implementing repair plans to allow for a safe return of visitors in spring 2027.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: John Stamos’ former California mansion drops from $13 million to $6.4 million after renovations
item.description: John Stamos’s luxurious California mansion has experienced substantial price drops since 2025. Initially, this Mediterranean-style estate in Calabasas was priced near $13 million, but after renovations by the current owners, it now stands at about $6.4 million. Stamos originally acquired the property in 1991 for $430,000 and sold it in 2001, illustrating the complexities in marketing highly personalized high-end real estate.
item.dc:creator: TOI Real Estate Desk

item.title: Philadelphia Orchestra marks 14th China tour with $10.5m gift for global tours and new music
item.description: David L Cohen and Rhonda R Cohen have made an impressive commitment of $10.5 million to the Philadelphia Orchestra. This significant donation aims to fund international tours and foster cultural exchanges, while also introducing new music initiatives worldwide. Their contribution will establish the Fund for Cultural Diplomacy, enhancing the orchestra's role as a cultural ambassador, alongside launching the Artistic Innovation and Discovery Fund to spotlight underrepresented composers.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Hendrie Ranch Conservation Easement: Florida approves $12.9m deal; wildlife corridor stays working
item.description: A 5,610-acre section of Hendrie Ranch will remain undeveloped due to a $12.9 million conservation easement. This agreement, approved by state officials, allows continued agricultural use while protecting the land from development. The ranch supports cattle, hay production, and timber harvesting alongside diverse wildlife habitats. It is part of Florida's Rural and Family Lands Protection Program to safeguard agricultural properties.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: New York man challenges bank over 2005 mortgage, wins appeal in foreclosure dispute
item.description: A New York homeowner who took out a mortgage in 2005 has secured a reversal of a foreclosure ruling that had favoured US Bank National Association. Moses Sukljian challenged the bank's right to enforce the loan after it accused him of missing payments. On Friday, an appeals court overturned the earlier ruling, finding that the bank had failed to provide sufficient proof of its legal standing.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: New York couple pledges $10 million to expand NICU after granddaughter’s birth experience
item.description: Donald and Barbara Zucker have pledged a remarkable $10 million to elevate the standard of neonatal intensive care at Good Samaritan University Hospital. This generous commitment will be complemented by donations from the community, amplifying its reach. The initiative aims to upgrade the neonatal unit with cutting-edge technology and supportive amenities, ensuring high-risk newborns and their families receive essential care in a nurturing environment close to home.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Texas student builds landscaping business to fund college, wins national agribusiness award
item.description: Texas student Jose Yepez started a landscaping business to pay for college, but it soon grew into a company serving more than 100 clients and employing four full-time workers. The business has also helped him support his family financially. His efforts earned him the 2026 American Star in Agribusiness award from the National FFA Organization on Friday.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Alabama lawyer gave up career to care for parents, but court upheld cancellation of her condo deed
item.description: The Alabama Supreme Court has affirmed a lower court's ruling that invalidated a property transfer from parents to their daughter, Holly Schumpert. Despite her dedication in caring for her ailing parents, the court determined the coastal condominium was part of a family trust, rendering the deed null. As a result, laws designed to protect elderly property owners allowed the reversal, leading to Holly having no claim to the estate.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: DNA evidence solves 2012 murder of North Carolina student Faith Hedgepeth, 14 years later
item.description: Miguel Salguero Olivares has received a life sentence for the chilling murder of Faith Hedgepeth, whose case remained a mystery for nearly ten years. Thanks to DNA evidence, he was arrested and convicted of first-degree murder, rape, and burglary. Faith's lifeless body was found in her apartment in September 2012 after a fun night out.

item.title: After years of abandonment, 48 acres once home to Ohio's SeaWorld and Six Flags parks are set to reopen on October 25
item.description: Aurora Park at Geauga Lake will reopen to the public on October 25, focusing on outdoor recreation. This redevelopment includes seating areas, boating access, and restored structures from the amusement park era. Future phases will introduce a public beach, playground, and other recreational facilities as part of the project. The City of Aurora acquired the property in December 2024 to ensure public access.
item.dc:creator: TOI Lifestyle Desk

item.title: Arctic ice had been expanding for 1,000 years before reaching its greatest extent around 1960
item.description: A recent study indicates that the Barnes Ice Cap had begun expanding nearly 2,000 years ago. This expansion was attributed to cooler summer conditions that allowed ice to grow. However, rising greenhouse gas emissions reversed this trend and caused significant ice retreat since the 1960s. Researchers emphasize that human-induced warming has disrupted natural climate patterns that favored renewed glacial growth.
